beats.lead: People usually just remember the line.
beats.text: 'just setting up my twttr' — posted 21 March 2006, before the product was even called Twitter.
beats.note: It launched publicly as Twitter four months later, in July 2006.

beats.name: 'stat.us'
beats.role: Jack Dorsey's own first sketch of the idea, drawn on a notepad five years earlier. Nothing came of it until Odeo, a podcasting company, gave the concept a real team in March 2006.

beats.text: Co-founder Noah Glass chose 'Twitter,' not Dorsey.
beats.note: He took it from the Oxford English Dictionary: 'a short inconsequential burst of information... chirps from birds.'

beats.lead: That tweet later became a very literal collector's item.
beats.text: Entrepreneur Sina Estavi bought it as an NFT for $2.9 million in March 2021.
beats.note: Dorsey converted the proceeds to bitcoin and donated them to charity.

beats.context: The top bid when Estavi tried to resell that same NFT for $48 million thirteen months later. Seven bids came in; none went higher.

beats.line: The internet's most expensive four words, and the crash that followed them.
